speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to Dr. Agent's office. I see you are presenting with knee pain after recently increasing your physical activity. To help me understand your condition, please describe exactly where the pain is located and what it feels like. Additionally, have you noticed any swelling, clicking, or instability in the knee?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the history of pivoting and twisting in volleyball is very suggestive of a specific injury mechanism. Given the worsening pain, did the knee give way or buckle at any point, and are you experiencing significant swelling or warmth around the joint? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Knee

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No fracture, dislocation, or appreciable joint effusion.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints). The patient's specific pain location over the medial tibia, combined with recent increased pivoting activity, strongly supports this diagnosis; the mention of pneumonia is clinically irrelevant to her knee symptoms.
